findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical shared-edge count: each land cell contributes four sides, and each previously seen land neighbor removes the two contributions of one internal edge. It scans the grid once, uses clear row and column names, and is expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 463 and its rectangular binary-grid Python contract. The O(rows * cols) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the nested scan and scalar perimeter; the protected source neither allocates traversal state nor mutates the grid.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064947898. Its row-major traversal, water skip, four-side addition, above-neighbor cancellation, left-neighbor cancellation, and returned perimeter are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only annotation spelling and the LeetCode wrapper differ.

The dense 8x8, 16x16, and 32x32 islands span 16x in cell count and force all land-cell and shared-edge work. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.95x the reference runtime. A correct control using linear list membership for every neighboring coordinate passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 7.64x.

The Approach exactly describes the protected four-sides-per-land-cell accounting, why checking only above and left counts each shared edge once, and why subtracting two removes both internal contributions. Its linear scan proof, constant-space bound, traversal alternatives, and border, narrow, and concave-shape boundaries are accurate.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the rectangular map model, orthogonal connectivity, surrounding water, single-island and no-lakes guarantees, unit-cell geometry, all three exact examples, and all five constraints. An accessible grid table independently reproduces the source image and exposes each cell's contribution to the stated perimeter of 16.
